=== ssh_proxy_cli 
exit 0
--- stdout
ssh_proxy_cli - SSH SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli [options] <command> [command options]

Commands:
  start               Start the proxy in the background
    [--foreground] [--wait SECONDS]  Foreground; wait defaults to 20s
  restart             Restart with the current configuration
    [--foreground] [--wait SECONDS]  Foreground; wait defaults to 20s
  stop                Stop the proxy and its SSH tunnel
  status              Show endpoint and health as JSON

  trust               Set up SSH login and host-key trust
    [--log FILE] [ENDPOINT_NAME]     Append diagnostics; select an endpoint
  logs                Show or follow proxy logs
    [--follow|-f] [--lines N]        Follow; last 60 lines by default
  test                Test HTTP and SOCKS5 forwarding
    [--url URL]                      Default: https://example.com/
  check               Validate configuration as JSON

  Use "ssh_proxy_cli <command> --help" for details and examples.

Service commands (current user):
  service install     Register and enable automatic startup
  service uninstall   Stop and remove the service
  service status      Show service state and automatic startup
  service enable      Enable automatic startup
  service disable     Disable automatic startup

  Permissions:
    Windows      Run service commands in an elevated terminal.
                 Install prompts for your Windows password.
    macOS/Linux  Run as the current user, without sudo.

  Use "ssh_proxy_cli service --help" for service details.

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help
  -v, --version       Print the version
--- stderr

=== ssh_proxy_cli start --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Start the proxy in the background

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli start [options]

Options:
  --foreground        Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  --wait SECONDS      Wait SECONDS for background readiness (default: 20)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent. Run trust for setup.
  After --wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness.
  --wait accepts 1..3600 seconds and has no effect with --foreground.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli start
  ssh_proxy_cli start --foreground
--- stderr

  --wait SECONDS      Wait SECONDS for background readiness (default: 20)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent. Run trust for setup.
  After --wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness.
  --wait accepts 1..3600 seconds and has no effect with --foreground.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli restart
  ssh_proxy_cli restart --wait 30

=== ssh_proxy_cli trust --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Set up SSH login and host-key trust

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli trust [options] [ENDPOINT_NAME]

Options:
  --check             Check unattended login only: no prompts or new host keys
  --log FILE          Append SSH diagnostics to FILE (used by the tray)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Without an endpoint, try SSH aliases in file order until one succeeds.
  Verify host fingerprints before accepting. Already working logins exit 0.
  --check fails instead of prompting; the tray runs it before each start.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli trust
  ssh_proxy_cli trust my-proxy
--- stderr
=== ssh_proxy_cli logs --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Show or follow proxy logs

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli logs [options]

Options:
  -f, --follow        Follow new log lines
  --lines N           Show the last N lines (default: 60)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  --lines accepts 1..10000. Output is plain text.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli logs
  ssh_proxy_cli logs --follow
--- stderr
=== ssh_proxy_cli test --help
exit 0
--- stdout
Test HTTP and SOCKS5 forwarding

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli test [options]

Options:
  --url URL           Fetch URL (default: https://example.com/)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  The proxy must be running. A failed check returns a nonzero exit code.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli test
  ssh_proxy_cli test --url https://example.com/

=== ssh_proxy_cli service
exit 0
--- stdout
Manage the proxy service for the current user

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli service <command> [options]

Commands:
  install             Register and enable automatic startup
  uninstall           Stop and remove the service
  status              Show service state and automatic startup
  enable              Enable automatic startup
  disable             Disable automatic startup

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Service behavior:
  Registration uses the current user on every OS.
  Install enables automatic startup without starting the proxy.
  Enable/disable change automatic startup; use start, stop or restart to run it.
  On macOS, re-enable a disabled service before starting it manually.

Permissions:
  Windows             Install, uninstall, enable and disable require elevation.
                      Install prompts for the current Windows account password.
  macOS/Linux         Run as the current user, without sudo.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli service install
  ssh_proxy_cli start
  ssh_proxy_cli service status
--- stderr

Restart with the current configuration

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli restart [options]

Options:
  --foreground        Run in this terminal; Ctrl+C stops the proxy
  --wait SECONDS      Wait SECONDS for background readiness (default: 20)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Background mode requires SSH keys or ssh-agent. Run trust for setup.
  After --wait expires, the proxy may keep retrying; check status for readiness.
  --wait accepts 1..3600 seconds and has no effect with --foreground.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli restart
  ssh_proxy_cli restart --wait 30

                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  The proxy must be running. A failed check returns a nonzero exit code.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli test
  ssh_proxy_cli test --url https://example.com/

flag needs an argument: -log
Set up SSH login and host-key trust

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli trust [options] [ENDPOINT_NAME]

Options:
  --check             Check unattended login only: no prompts or new host keys
  --log FILE          Append SSH diagnostics to FILE (used by the tray)

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Without an endpoint, try SSH aliases in file order until one succeeds.
  Verify host fingerprints before accepting. Already working logins exit 0.
  --check fails instead of prompting; the tray runs it before each start.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli trust
  ssh_proxy_cli trust my-proxy
Error: flag needs an argument: -log

flag provided but not defined: -user
Register and enable automatic startup

Usage:
  ssh_proxy_cli service install [options]

Global options:
  -c, --config PATH   Read configuration from PATH
                      (default: config.toml beside the executable)
  -h, --help          Show help

Notes:
  Run trust and confirm unattended login works, then stop before installing.

Service behavior:
  Registration uses the current user on every OS.
  Install enables automatic startup without starting the proxy.
  Enable/disable change automatic startup; use start, stop or restart to run it.
  On macOS, re-enable a disabled service before starting it manually.

Permissions:
  Windows             Install, uninstall, enable and disable require elevation.
                      Install prompts for the current Windows account password.
  macOS/Linux         Run as the current user, without sudo.

Examples:
  ssh_proxy_cli service install
  ssh_proxy_cli start
Error: flag provided but not defined: -user
